title: International Bank For Reconstruction And Development
definition: The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) is an international financial institution established in 1944, functioning as the original lending arm of the World Bank Group to promote sustainable development, poverty reduction, and institution building in middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries.
importanceInUpsc: Frequently tested in UPSC Prelims regarding international financial architectures, voting rights, and World Bank Group components; essential for Mains GS Paper III (Global economic governance, international institutions, and developmental financing).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of International Bank For Reconstruction And Development.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of Bretton Woods institutions
Basics of international monetary and financial systems
